title: 70% Chance of Rain? Probability Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
The weather report says 70 percent chance of rain tomorrow. But tomorrow it will either rain or it will not, so what does 70 percent mean? And why is no rain exactly 30 percent? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 14, Probability) we learn events and the axioms of probability.

You will watch a die thrown 600 times while the share of even numbers settles near one half, then meet the sample space, events, not E, E or F, E and F, and mutually exclusive events on six die tiles. Step by step we build the three NCERT axioms, P(E) ≥ 0, P(S) = 1 and the addition rule for mutually exclusive events, and use them to explain why P(no rain) = 1 - P(rain). A side-by-side of exclusive and overlapping events, a pause-and-think question, a worked example with P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B), the exam trap of counting the overlap twice, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
